title: [t2_single_node_max] Fix Indexing Error when PortChannels are Absent in LT2 VMs
author: arista-hpandya
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

The pick_ports function in the sonic-mgmt test framework currently contains an underlying assumption that portA (a valid interface connection) will always be found when searching for specific connection types, such as a PortChannel linked to downstream T1/LT2 VMs.

This assumption leads to indexing errors when the function is unable to find an interface that satisfies the search criteria. This is particularly evident in topologies like t2_single_node_max, where the downstream links do not utilize PortChannels, causing the pick_ports function to fail when it attempts to access a non-existent portA index.

Impact: The test suite fails when executed on topologies lacking the required PortChannel configuration, preventing successful test completion for valid scenarios where PortChannels are not utilized for downstream links.

### Steps to Reproduce

- Setup a t2_single_node_max topology
- Run any of the given tests listed below in the logs

Note: The requirement to reproduce is none of the downstream connections should be a portchannel as specified in t2_single_node_max topo.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual: The tests fail with an error: `KeyError: 'portA'`

Expected: We expect the tests to skip with an explicit message saying that no suitable portA was found

linkedPullRequests.title: Add check to verify if portA key exists in the pick_ports method
linkedPullRequests.author: arista-hpandya
linkedPullRequests.body:
In pick_ports we assume portA always exists and this causes indexing errors. There may be cases where portA is not found, for example, when the test looks for a portchannel connected to downstream T1/LT2 VMs. In t2_single_node_max the downstream links do not have portchannels, and hence no intf will satisfy this condition.

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
The pick_ports function assumes that portA always exists after attempting to find a connection that satisfies specific criteria (e.g., a PortChannel connected to downstream T1/LT2 VMs).

In topologies like t2_single_node_max, the downstream links do not have PortChannels, meaning no interface satisfies the condition. This leads to an IndexError when the code tries to access portA, causing the test execution to fail unexpectedly. This PR fixes the pick_ports failure in these scenarios.

#### How did you do it?
Modified the pick_ports function to gracefully handle cases where no interface matching the required criteria is found, preventing the indexing error.

#### How did you verify/test it?
The changes were verified by running the affected test suite on the t2_single_node_max topology. The test no longer crashes due to the indexing error in pick_ports and are skipped as expected when downstream PortChannels are absent.

comments.author: Javier-Tan
comments.body:
Triaged the same bug and came to a similar conclusion. This fix would definitely solve the issue.

However I'm not sure if it would be better to explicitly check each DUT for a suitable portchannel/interface in case there is a future chassis T2 topology where it could possibly reach a 2nd suitable DUT.

e.g. 1st DUT doesn't have a suitable portA, but 2nd DUT does

For example, replacing old L234-239:

```
        # Check if at least one port of type port_type_a exists in the downlink (T1/LT2 neighbors)
        port_type_a_intf_exists = False
        for _, intfs in list(portT1_neigh.items()):
            for intf in intfs:
                port_type_a_intf_exists = (port_type_a == "ethernet" and intf.startswith("Ethernet")) or \
                                          (port_type_a == "portchannel" and intf.startswith("PortChannel"))
                if port_type_a_intf_exists:
                    break

        if dutA and port_type_a_intf_exists:
            break
        elif dutA:
            logger.info("Found DUT {} with downlink (T1/LT2) neighbors, but contains no ports of type {}"
                        .format(dutA, port_type_a))
            dutA = None

    if dutA is None:
        pytest.skip("Did not find any asic in the DUTs (linecards) "
                    "that are connected to downlink (T1/LT2) VM's OR "
                    "did not find any downlink (T1/LT2) ports of type {}".format(port_type_a))
```
